title: B-Cell Clones on Flow: Restriction, MBL, CLL and Hematogones
summary: Learn what light-chain restriction does and does not prove, how CLL-phenotype B-cell counts separate MBL from CLL, and how hematogones differ from lymphoblasts on flow cytometry.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 35 Hit 6 (CLL/SLL phenotype and the 5,000/μL MBL boundary), Hit 12 (hematogones), Hit 14 (kappa or lambda; restriction = clonality), Trap 3 (clonality is not neoplasia) and Trap 5 (hematogones mistaken for B-ALL relapse). Checked against WHO-HAEM5 (Alaggio 2022), the ERIC/ESCCA CLL harmonisation (Rawstron 2018), Gajzer & Fromm 2025, Galigalidou 2021, Quinquenel 2020 (FILO), Chiattone 2025, Singh 2023, Carulli 2014, Guillory 2016 and Pauza 1993. Qualified: Hit 14 “never both” and “restriction proves clonality” (Pauza 1993 kappa+/lambda+ normal fetal B cells; Guillory 2016 lambda-restricted hematogones without molecular clonality) and Hit 6 (WHO-HAEM5 also requires no other features of CLL/SLL and splits low-count from CLL-type MBL; SLL does not need the 5,000/μL count). Pending: reactive clonal T-cell expansions.

objectives: Explain what kappa/lambda light-chain restriction shows and why clonality alone is not neoplasia.
Classify a CLL-phenotype B-cell clone as low-count MBL, CLL-type MBL or in the CLL range by its count.
Distinguish hematogones from lymphoblasts by their maturation pattern on flow cytometry.

scenes.title: Three B-cell puzzles
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three flow cytometry reports. (1) A 4-year-old on day 28 after induction for B-lymphoblastic leukaemia: marrow shows 14% blast-like CD19+/CD10+ cells. (2) A 72-year-old with a routine blood count: CD5+/CD19+/CD23+ B cells with dim CD20 and dim lambda only, 3,000/μL, no other findings. (3) A lymph node: kappa-restricted B cells with an otherwise normal immunophenotype. Question token: “Relapse, leukaemia, lymphoma, or benign?”

cues.text: Three flow reports. A four-year-old, day twenty-eight after leukaemia induction, with fourteen percent blast-like CD19 and CD10 positive cells in the marrow.
A seventy-two-year-old with three thousand CLL-like B cells per microlitre and nothing else wrong. And a lymph node with kappa-only B cells that otherwise look normal.
Relapse, leukaemia, lymphoma, or something benign?

scenes.title: What normal B cells look like
scenes.altText: Schematic. Left card: a normal mature B-cell population is a mix of kappa-bearing and lambda-bearing cells, roughly 1.5 kappa to 1 lambda. Right card: the hematogone ladder in marrow — stage 1: CD34+, TdT+, CD38+, CD19+, bright CD10, CD20−, dimmest CD45; stage 2: CD34 and TdT lost, CD10 partly down, CD20 rising; stage 3: more CD20 and surface light chains appear; mature B cell: CD10 off, bright CD20, CD45 brighter. Token: hematogones are increased in young children and in regenerating marrow after chemotherapy or transplant.

cues.text: Normal mature B cells are a mixed crowd. Most cells show one light chain, kappa or lambda, and a reactive population mixes both, roughly one and a half kappa to one lambda.
In the marrow, hematogones are normal B-cell precursors. The earliest express CD34, TdT, CD19, CD38 and bright CD10, without CD20, and have the dimmest CD45.
As they mature they lose CD34 and TdT, gain CD20 step by step, and acquire surface light chains last, while CD45 grows brighter.
Hematogones are most prominent in young children and expand in regenerating marrow after chemotherapy or transplant.

scenes.title: Clone, cancer, or neither?
scenes.altText: Three cards. Card 1, light-chain restriction: a B-cell population skewed to one light chain is clonal. Card 2, clonal is not the same as malignant: reactive B-cell clones occur in Hashimoto thyroiditis and follicular hyperplasia; monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis occurs in otherwise healthy people (more than 20% of people over 70); reactive clones tend to keep an otherwise normal immunophenotype, while neoplastic B cells show aberrant expression of other antigens (for example CD5, CD10, CD38, CD45). Card 3, blasts versus hematogones: lymphoblasts show aberrancies such as uniform TdT and CD34, low CD45, CD20, HLA-DR or CD38, overexpressed CD10, or CD34 with CD20 together; hematogones form a smooth maturation continuum, often two to three dim-CD45 clusters rather than one.

cues.text: A B-cell population skewed to a single light chain is light-chain restricted, which points to a clone.

But a clone is not automatically a cancer. Reactive B-cell clones occur in Hashimoto thyroiditis and in follicular hyperplasia, and monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis is found in more than a fifth of healthy people over seventy.
The clue is the rest of the phenotype. Reactive clones usually look otherwise normal; neoplastic B cells show aberrant expression of antigens such as CD5, CD10, CD38 or CD45.

The same logic separates lymphoblasts from hematogones. Blasts show aberrancies: uniform TdT and CD34, low CD45, CD20 or CD38, overbright CD10, or CD34 and CD20 together. Hematogones show a smooth, orderly maturation pattern.

scenes.title: CLL phenotype and the count
scenes.altText: Card 1, CLL/SLL phenotype (ERIC/ESCCA required panel): CD19+, CD5+, CD23+, weak CD20, weak and restricted kappa or lambda; useful extra markers CD43, CD79b, CD81, CD200, CD10, ROR1; CD200 bright and FMC7 dim to absent. Card 2, the count of clonal CLL-phenotype B cells: below 0.5 × 10⁹/L = low-count MBL; 0.5 to under 5 × 10⁹/L with no other features of CLL/SLL = CLL-type (high-count) MBL; 5 × 10⁹/L (5,000/μL) is the CLL boundary. Hook answers: (1) orderly maturation = hematogones, not relapse; (2) 3,000/μL with nothing else = CLL-type MBL, not CLL; (3) clonal but phenotypically normal = not lymphoma on that finding alone; correlate clinically.

cues.text: The CLL phenotype: CD19, CD5 and CD23 positive, with weak CD20 and weak, restricted kappa or lambda. CD200 is bright and FMC7 is dim to absent; CD43, CD79b, CD81 and ROR1 help in borderline cases.

Then count the clone. Under half a billion per litre is low-count MBL. From half a billion up to five billion per litre, with no other features of CLL, it is CLL-type MBL. Five billion per litre, five thousand per microlitre, is the CLL boundary.
Back to the hook. The child’s orderly maturation pattern means hematogones, not relapse. The adult’s three thousand per microlitre, with nothing else, is CLL-type MBL.
The lymph node clone looks otherwise normal, so restriction alone does not make it lymphoma: correlate with morphology and the clinical picture.

props.title: CLL/SLL phenotype
lines: Weak CD20 · weak κ or λ

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Light-chain restriction = lymphoma” (✓ clonality alone is not neoplasia; look for an aberrant phenotype and clinical context); “CD10+/TdT+ cells after chemotherapy = relapse” (✓ hematogones expand in regenerating marrow and mature in an orderly way); “A CLL phenotype means CLL” (✓ below 5 × 10⁹/L clonal B cells without other CLL/SLL features it is MBL).

cues.text: Trap one: light-chain restriction means lymphoma. No: a clone can be reactive or MBL. Look for an aberrant phenotype and the clinical picture.
Trap two: CD10 and TdT positive cells after chemotherapy mean relapse. No: regenerating hematogones mature in an orderly way; blasts show aberrancies.
Trap three: a CLL phenotype means CLL. No: below five thousand clonal B cells per microlitre, with no other features of CLL, it is MBL.

props.title: ✗ “κ-restricted = lymphoma.”
lines: ✓ Clone ≠ cancer; look for aberrant phenotype

scenes.title: Choir, soloist, staircase
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Normal B cells are a CHOIR singing two parts, kappa and lambda. A clone is a SOLOIST — but a soloist is not a criminal unless it sings wrong notes (aberrant antigens). Hematogones climb the STAIRCASE in order; blasts are stuck on a wrong step.” Tokens: choir = polyclonal · soloist = clone · staircase = hematogones. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: normal B cells are a choir singing two parts, kappa and lambda. A clone is a soloist, but a soloist is not a criminal unless it sings wrong notes. Hematogones climb the staircase in order; blasts are stuck on a wrong step.

Where it breaks: a few normal fetal B cells show both light chains; hematogones have rarely been reported as light-chain restricted; CLL cells may show so little surface light chain that restriction is hard to see; and the count thresholds are arbitrary.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Restriction = clone · clone ≠ cancer · look for aberrant antigens”, “Hematogones mature in order · CLL-phenotype under 5,000/μL alone = MBL”.

cues.text: Light-chain restriction marks a clone but not a cancer, so look for aberrant antigens, remember that hematogones mature in an orderly way, and call a CLL-phenotype clone under 5,000 per microlitre without other features monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis.

props.label: Restriction = clone · clone ≠ cancer · look for aberrant antigens
Hematogones mature in order · CLL-type clone < 5,000/μL alone = MBL

explanation.what: Plain language: healthy B cells are a mix of two light-chain types; a group of cells that all carry the same one is a clone. A clone is not always cancer, so the lab also checks whether the cells look abnormal in other ways and how many there are. Young, normal B-cell precursors (hematogones) can look like leukaemia cells under the microscope but mature in a tidy order on flow. Scientific terms: kappa/lambda light chains, light-chain restriction, clonality, aberrant immunophenotype, monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL; low-count and CLL-type), chronic lymphocytic leukaemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL), hematogones (stage 1–3 B-cell precursors), lymphoblasts.
explanation.why: A reactive B-cell population mixes kappa and lambda, so a strongly skewed ratio implies a clone. Neoplastic B cells usually also show abnormal expression of other antigens, while reactive clones and hematogones keep a normal pattern. MBL is defined by a clonal count below the CLL boundary in an otherwise healthy person, and it is common in older adults.
explanation.measure: Reactive kappa:lambda about 1.5:1. CLL required markers (ERIC/ESCCA): CD19, CD5, CD20 (weak), CD23, kappa, lambda (weak and restricted); recommended CD43, CD79b, CD81, CD200, CD10, ROR1. Clonal CLL-phenotype B cells: < 0.5 × 10⁹/L low-count MBL; 0.5 to < 5 × 10⁹/L with no other CLL/SLL features CLL-type MBL; 5 × 10⁹/L = 5,000/μL. Hematogones: stage 1 CD34+/TdT+/CD10 bright/CD20−; then CD34 and TdT lost, CD20 rising, surface light chains last.
explanation.differs: Clonal vs neoplastic; reactive clone (normal phenotype) vs lymphoma (aberrant CD5, CD10, CD38, CD45); MBL vs CLL (count and other features); CLL vs SLL (SLL: lymphadenopathy and/or splenomegaly without a leukaemic clonal count, diagnosed on lymph node biopsy); hematogones (orderly continuum, several dim-CD45 clusters) vs lymphoblasts (uniform TdT/CD34, abnormal CD45/CD20/CD38/CD10).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: interpret a kappa-restricted but otherwise normal population, classify a CLL-phenotype count as MBL or CLL, or recognise hematogones in a post-chemotherapy marrow.

comparisons.title: Reactive clone vs neoplastic clone

right.label: Neoplastic clone
points: Aberrant CD5, CD10, CD38 or CD45

comparisons.distinguisher: Aberrant expression of antigens other than the light chain, plus clinical context.

comparisons.title: Hematogones vs lymphoblasts

left.label: Hematogones
points: Orderly CD34 → CD20 → surface light chain

comparisons.distinguisher: Smooth maturation continuum vs an arrested, aberrant phenotype.

mnemonic.text: Normal B cells are a CHOIR singing two parts, kappa and lambda. A clone is a SOLOIST, but a soloist is not a criminal unless it sings wrong notes (aberrant antigens). Hematogones climb the STAIRCASE in order; blasts are stuck on a wrong step.
mnemonic.explanation: Separates polyclonal, clonal and neoplastic B cells, and orderly from arrested maturation.
mnemonic.limitation: A small fraction of normal fetal B cells co-express kappa and lambda; hematogones have rarely been reported as light-chain restricted; CLL cells can have so little surface light chain that restriction is hard to show; count thresholds are arbitrary.

analogyLimitations: Cell and plot drawings are schematic.
Thresholds follow WHO-HAEM5; other classifications or local practice may differ.
takeaway: Light-chain restriction marks a clone but not a cancer, so look for aberrant antigens, remember that hematogones mature in an orderly way, and call a CLL-phenotype clone under 5,000 per microlitre without other features monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old’s day-28 marrow after induction for B-lymphoblastic leukaemia shows 12% blast-like cells. Flow shows CD19+/CD10+ cells forming a continuum from CD34+/TdT+/CD20− cells to CD20+ cells with surface light chains, with no aberrant antigens. What is the best interpretation?

options.rationale: Correct. Orderly maturation from CD34+/TdT+ to CD20+ with light chains last, without aberrancies, is the hematogone pattern.
Incorrect. Blasts show aberrancies such as uniform TdT/CD34 or abnormal CD45, CD20, CD38 or CD10, not a smooth continuum.
Incorrect. CLL cells are mature CD5+/CD23+ B cells with restricted light chain, not CD34+/TdT+ precursors.
Incorrect. MBL is a clonal mature B-cell population in blood; these are normal B-cell precursors maturing in the marrow.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old has 2,500/μL clonal B cells that are CD5+, CD19+, CD23+, dim CD20 and dim kappa only, with no lymphadenopathy, organomegaly or cytopenias. Using WHO-HAEM5 categories, what is the classification?

options.rationale: Correct. 2.5 × 10⁹/L is between 0.5 and 5 × 10⁹/L with no other CLL/SLL features.
Incorrect. The clonal count is below 5 × 10⁹/L (5,000/μL) and there are no other CLL/SLL features.
Incorrect. Kappa-only cells with a CLL phenotype are clonal, not polyclonal.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry on a lymph node shows a kappa-restricted B-cell population whose other antigens are expressed normally. What is the best conclusion?

options.text: A clonal population; neoplasia is not established without an aberrant phenotype and clinical correlation
options.rationale: Correct. Reactive B-cell clones occur, for example in follicular hyperplasia, and tend to keep an otherwise normal phenotype.
Incorrect. Clonality alone is not neoplasia.
Incorrect. A population restricted to one light chain is clonal, not polyclonal.
Incorrect. Hematogones are marrow B-cell precursors that typically lack surface light chains.

claims.text: Reactive B cells mix kappa and lambda (about 1.5:1); a skewed, single-light-chain population is clonal; a few normal fetal B cells co-express both.
Clonality is not neoplasia: reactive B clones (Hashimoto thyroiditis, follicular hyperplasia) and MBL; reactive clones keep a normal phenotype, neoplasms show aberrant antigens; MBL in > 20% over 70.
CLL phenotype: required and recommended markers; bright CD200, dim/absent FMC7, dim light chain.
Low-count MBL < 0.5 × 10⁹/L; CLL-type MBL 0.5 to < 5 × 10⁹/L without other CLL/SLL features; 5 × 10⁹/L boundary.
claims.note: WHO-HAEM5 states the upper MBL limit as a total B-cell count < 5 × 10⁹/L; Galigalidou 2021 as 0.5–4.99 × 10⁹ clonal B cells/L; FILO 2020 and the Brazilian 2025 guideline word the CLL count as more than 5 × 10⁹/L clonal B lymphocytes.

claims.text: Hematogone maturation stages, settings (young children, regenerating marrow) and dim-CD45 pattern; light chains typically absent, rare restricted case.
Lymphoblast aberrancies vs normal B-cell precursors.
SLL: lymphadenopathy and/or splenomegaly without a leukaemic clonal count, diagnosed on lymph node biopsy.

claims.note: Not taught; no open source read in this session covers clonal T-cell expansions.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 35 Hit 14 says normal B cells express kappa OR lambda, “never both”. Pauza 1993 found normal fetal B cells co-expressing surface kappa and lambda at 2–3% of surface-Ig+ B cells; Guillory 2016 also describes lambda-restricted hematogones with no clonal IG rearrangement by PCR, so flow restriction does not always prove clonality. The lesson teaches “most cells show one light chain” and treats restriction as a population-level pointer to a clone (register flag rv-ch35-kappa-lambda-dual).

Ch. 35 Hit 6 says a CLL-phenotype count below 5,000/μL “is MBL”. WHO-HAEM5 requires no other features diagnostic of CLL/SLL, separates low-count MBL (< 0.5 × 10⁹/L) from CLL-type MBL, and states the upper limit as total B cells < 5 × 10⁹/L. Hit 6 also says “CLL/SLL needs ≥5,000”, but SLL is diagnosed without the leukaemic count, on lymphadenopathy and/or splenomegaly with lymph node biopsy (Chiattone 2025) (register flag rv-ch35-mbl-other-features).
